cards.text: It's Passover night, and Jesus is at the table with His apostles. He's just told them the hand of His betrayer is right there on the table with His. So they start asking each other which of them could ever do it.
Then the talk at that table takes a turn. A dispute breaks out among the disciples.

cards.question: At the Passover table, a dispute breaks out among the disciples. What is it about?

answers.text: Which of them should be considered the greatest
Which of them should lead the Passover prayer
Which of them should go out to buy supplies

cards.text: I'm the only one on my whole planet, and friend, I STILL lose arguments with my oven about who's in charge. Then Jesus steps in: the kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority call themselves benefactors.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples they should be like the kings of the Gentiles.

cards.text: Instead, Jesus flips the whole ladder upside down. The greatest among them should be like the youngest.

cards.question: Jesus says the one who leads should be like the one who ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks who's greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves. And He answers it Himself: “Is it not the one who reclines?”

cards.question: Jesus says the one who reclines at the table is greater than the one who serves. So how does He describe Himself among the disciples?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to them. They're the ones, He says, who have stood by Him in His trials.

cards.question: Jesus bestows a kingdom on the disciples, just as His ___ has bestowed one on Him.
Jesus bestows a kingdom on the disciples. What does He say they'll do in His kingdom?

answers.text: Eat and drink at His table
Guard the gates of the city

cards.text: His table in His kingdom, AND they'll sit on thrones? Friend, when I argue with my oven, I don't get a throne. I get a burnt batch.

cards.question: From those thrones in the kingdom, the disciples will be judging the ___ tribes of Israel.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to Simon Peter, one of the Twelve. “Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat.”

cards.question: Satan has asked to sift the disciples like wheat. What has Jesus done for Simon?

answers.text: Prayed that his faith will not fail
Sent an angel to stand guard over him
Told him to hide until morning comes

cards.text: And Jesus gives Simon a job. When he has turned back, he's to strengthen his brothers.

cards.question: Peter answers Jesus. How far does he say he's ready to go with Him?

answers.text: Even to prison and to death
Even through the storm and the sea
Even into the desert and the wild

cards.text: Prison AND death, and friend, it took me a whole WEEK to commit to sprinkles! But Jesus answers Peter with a word about a rooster.

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter the rooster will not crow today until Peter has denied ___ times that he knows Him.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks them all a question. Back when He sent them out without purse or bag or sandals, did they lack anything?

cards.question: Jesus asks if the disciples lacked anything when He sent them out without purse or bag or sandals. What do they answer?

cards.text: Nothing, and friend, I pack three spare aprons just to walk across my own bakery! But now, Jesus tells them, things are different.

cards.question: Now Jesus tells the one with a purse to leave it behind.
Jesus says the one without a sword should sell his ___ and buy one.

cards.text: Then Jesus points to a Scripture about Himself: “And He was numbered with the transgressors.”

cards.question: Jesus says what is written about Him is reaching its fulfillment.

cards.text: The disciples speak up. They've got something to show Jesus.

cards.question: The disciples say, Look Lord, here are ___ swords.
The disciples show Jesus two swords. What does He answer?

cards.text: And that's where the table talk ends for now. But friend, this night is just getting started.

findings.problem: Card 1 says it's Passover night and names Jesus' companions as apostles. Those facts come from Luke 22:7-15, but the card cites only Luke 22:21-23.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Which of them could ever do it" adds disbelief that isn't in Luke 22:23, which says they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question links the two statements with "So," as if Jesus' self-description follows from the one who reclines being greater. Luke 22:27 sets them against each other with "But I am among you as one who serves." The wording reverses the connection the text gives and nudges the baker toward "As one who reclines."

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke "when I argue with my oven, I don't get a throne" suggests the disciples got thrones after arguing. In the text, the thrones follow from standing by Jesus in His trials (Luke 22:28-30), not from the dispute. The core action of the comparison (arguing, then getting a reward) doesn't match the core action of the fact.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Simon Peter, one of the Twelve" states a fact from outside the passage (Luke 6:13-14) without its reference. The card cites only Luke 22:31.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No earlier card gives the baker a way to reason out "That is enough." Jesus has just told them to buy swords, so "Bring Me more" looks like the logical pick, and the right answer can only be found by luck. Stop 2 already leans on several discovery questions (cards 11 and 15), so this one should get more setup or be asked differently.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
